title.zh: 卷286 列傳七十三 王掞 劳之辨 朱天保 陶彝
title.en: Volume 286 Biographies 73: Wang Shan, Lao Zhibian, Zhu Tianbao, Tao Yi
title.raw: 卷286 列傳七十三 王掞 劳之辨 朱天保 陶彝

sentences.zh: 列傳七十三

translations.literal: Biographies 73
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 73

sentences.zh: 王掞子奕清奕鴻勞之辨硃天保陶彝任坪范長發鄒圖雲

translations.literal: Wang Shan; his sons Yiqing and Yihong; Lao Zhibian; Zhu Tianbao; Tao Yi; Ren Ping; Fan Changfa; Zou Tuyun
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shan; his sons Yiqing and Yihong; Lao Zhibian; Zhu Tianbao; Tao Yi; Ren Ping; Fan Changfa; and Zou Tuyun

sentences.zh: 陳嘉猷王允晉李允符範允高玢高怡趙成麃孫紹曾邵璿

translations.literal: Chen Jiayou, Wang Yunjin, Li Yunfu, Fan Yun, Gao Bin, Gao Yi, Zhao Chengbiao, Sun Shaozeng, and Shao Xuan
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jiayou, Wang Yunjin, Li Yunfu, Fan Yun, Gao Bin, Gao Yi, Zhao Chengbiao, Sun Shaozeng, and Shao Xuan

sentences.zh: 王掞，字藻儒，江南太倉人，明大學士錫爵孫。

translations.literal: Wang Shan, style Zaosru, was a native of Taicang in Jiangnan; he was the grandson of Xijue, Grand Secretary of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shan, whose style was Zaosru, came from Taicang in Jiangnan. He was the grandson of the Ming Grand Secretary Xijue.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，為掌院學士熊賜履所器。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of the Kangxi reign he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler; he was esteemed by Xiong Cili, the academy's chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1670 he became a metropolitan graduate, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was made a compiler. Chancellor Xiong Cili held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 遷左贊善，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent and served as an officer of the Daily Lecture and Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent and appointed to the Daily Lecture and Imperial Diary.

sentences.zh: 以病告八年，起右贊善。

translations.literal: He resigned on grounds of illness for eight years, then was recalled as Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years' leave for illness, he was recalled as Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 提督浙江學政，嚴剔積弊，所拔多宿學寒畯。

translations.literal: As educational commissioner of Zhejiang, he rigorously eliminated long-standing abuses; most of those he advanced were veteran scholars of humble birth.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhejiang educational commissioner, he rooted out entrenched abuses and chiefly promoted seasoned scholars from poor families.

sentences.zh: 龍泉知縣茅國璽以印揭薦武童，掞疏劾，國璽坐譴，別疏陳剔除積弊，報聞。

translations.literal: Mao Guoxi, magistrate of Longquan, used an official seal on a memorial to recommend a military candidate; Shan memorialized in impeachment, and Guoxi was punished. In a separate memorial he set forth the elimination of accumulated abuses; the court was informed.
translations.idiomatic: When Longquan magistrate Mao Guoxi used his official seal to recommend a military candidate, Shan impeached him and Mao was punished. Shan also submitted a separate memorial on rooting out abuses, which the throne acknowledged.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 三十年，超擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was promoted by special selection to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1691 he was specially promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，遷戶部侍郎，直經筵。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and attended the Classics Lecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1694 he became Vice Minister of Revenue and continued to attend the imperial lecture.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，調吏部，禁革臨選駁查、臨掣買簽諸弊，銓政以肅。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, forbade and abolished such abuses as last-minute rejection of candidates, last-minute drawing of lots, and buying appointments; personnel administration was thereby rectified.
translations.idiomatic: In 1699 he moved to the Ministry of Personnel, banned abuses such as last-minute rejections, rigged lot-drawing, and purchased appointments, and brought the civil service roster under order.

sentences.zh: 偕尚書范承勳、王鴻緒督修高家堰河工。

translations.literal: Together with Ministers Fan Chengxun and Wang Hongxu he supervised repairs on the Gaojia Embankment river works.
translations.idiomatic: With Ministers Fan Chengxun and Wang Hongxu he oversaw repairs on the Gaojia Embankment.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，擢刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was promoted to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In 1704 he was appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 刑部奏讞無漢字供狀，掞言：「本朝官制，兼設滿、漢，欲其彼此參詳。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice reported a verdict without a Chinese-language deposition. Shan said: "Our dynasty's official system sets up both Manchu and Han posts, intending that they consult each other.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry reported a verdict with no Chinese deposition, Shan said: "In our dynasty Manchu and Han officials serve side by side so that each may review the other.

sentences.zh: 今獄詞不錄漢語，是非曲直，漢司官何由知之？

translations.literal: Now if the case record does not include Chinese, how are Han officials to know right from wrong?
translations.idiomatic: If the record omits Chinese, how can Han officials judge right from wrong?

sentences.zh: 若隨聲畫諾，幾成虛設。

translations.literal: If they merely echo assent, their posts are nearly empty titles.
translations.idiomatic: If they only nod along, their offices are reduced to empty names.

sentences.zh: 嗣後定讞，當滿、漢稿並具。」

translations.literal: Henceforth in fixing verdicts, Manchu and Han drafts should both be prepared."
translations.idiomatic: From now on verdicts should be drawn up in both Manchu and Chinese."

sentences.zh: 詔報可，著為令。

translations.literal: The edict approved and made it a standing regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and issued it as a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 累歷工、兵、禮諸部，務總紀綱，持大體。

translations.literal: He successively served in the Ministries of Works, War, and Rites, always keeping to the overall framework and upholding the larger principles.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn at Works, War, and Rites, always keeping the broad framework in view and holding to principle.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，授文淵閣大學士，兼禮部尚書，直經筵如故。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and concurrently Minister of Rites, attending the Classics Lecture as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 1712 he became Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and concurrent Minister of Rites, and continued at the imperial lecture as before.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，典會試。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1713 he presided over the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 其冬，以疾疏辭閣務，溫旨慰留。

translations.literal: That winter, citing illness, he memorialized to resign from Grand Secretariat duties; a gracious edict urged him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he asked to leave the Grand Secretariat on grounds of illness, but the emperor warmly urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 越年春，疾愈，仍入直。

translations.literal: The following spring, recovered, he resumed attendance at court.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring, recovered, he returned to regular duty at court.

sentences.zh: 孝惠章皇后祔太廟，議者欲祔於孝康章皇后之次，掞曰：「孝康章皇后雖母以子貴，然孝惠章皇后，章皇帝嫡配也，上聖孝格天。

translations.literal: When Empress Xiaohui was to be enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, deliberators wished to place her after Empress Xiaokang. Shan said: "Although Empress Xiaokang was honored as mother through her son, Empress Xiaohui was the lawful consort of Emperor Zhang; His Majesty's filial piety moves Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xiaohui was to be installed in the Ancestral Temple, some proposed placing her after Empress Xiaokang. Shan said: "Empress Xiaokang was honored as mother through her son, yet Empress Xiaohui was the lawful consort of Emperor Zhang, and the emperor's filial devotion reaches Heaven.

sentences.zh: 曩者太皇太后祔廟時，不以躋孝端文皇后之上，今肯以孝康章皇后躋孝惠章皇后上乎？」

translations.literal: When the Grand Empress Dowager was enshrined, she was not placed above Empress Xiaoduan; would His Majesty now place Empress Xiaokang above Empress Xiaohui?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Empress Dowager was enshrined, she was not ranked above Empress Xiaoduan. Would the throne now rank Empress Xiaokang above Empress Xiaohui?"

sentences.zh: 禮部不從，上果以為非，令改正。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites did not agree, but the emperor indeed held it wrong and ordered correction.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites disagreed, but the emperor found the plan improper and ordered it changed.

sentences.zh: 時上春秋高，皇太子允礽既廢，儲位未定。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was advanced in years; the Crown Prince Yunreng had already been deposed and the succession was unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then in advanced age. Crown Prince Yunreng had been deposed and the succession remained unsettled.

sentences.zh: 掞年七十馀，自念受恩深，又以其祖錫爵在明神宗朝，以建儲事受惡名，欲幹其蠱。

translations.literal: Shan was over seventy; reflecting on the deep favor he had received, and that his grandfather Xijue had borne an ill name in the Ming under Shenzong for urging the establishment of an heir, he wished to dispel that curse.
translations.idiomatic: Shan was over seventy. Mindful of the deep favor he had received, and that his grandfather Xijue had been vilified under the Ming Shenzong for pressing the heir question, he hoped to lift that family shadow.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，密奏請建儲，疏入，留中。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he submitted a secret memorial requesting the establishment of an heir; the memorial was received but held back.
translations.idiomatic: In 1717 he secretly memorialized to name an heir. The memorial was received but not acted upon.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，御史陳嘉猷等八人復以為言，上不悅，遂並發掞疏，命內閣議處。

translations.literal: That winter Censor Chen Jiayou and seven others again spoke on the matter; the emperor was displeased, released Shan's memorial together with theirs, and ordered the Grand Secretariat to deliberate punishment.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Censor Chen Jiayou and seven others raised the issue again. Displeased, the emperor released Shan's memorial with theirs and ordered the Grand Secretariat to decide his punishment.

sentences.zh: 忌掞者欲置重典，掞止宮門外不敢入。

translations.literal: Those who resented Shan wished to impose severe penalties; Shan stopped outside the palace gate and dared not enter.
translations.idiomatic: His enemies sought a heavy sentence. Shan halted outside the palace gate and did not dare enter.

sentences.zh: 上顧左右，問：「王掞何在？」

translations.literal: The emperor looked to those beside him and asked: "Where is Wang Shan?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked about and asked, "Where is Wang Shan?"

sentences.zh: ​​李光地奏掞待罪宮門。

translations.literal: Li Guangdi reported that Shan was awaiting judgment at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi reported that Shan was waiting outside the gate to accept punishment.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「王掞言甚是，但不宜令御史同奏，蹈明季惡習。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Wang Shan's words are very much to the point, but he should not have had censors submit together with him, reviving the evil custom of late Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wang Shan is quite right, but he should not have had censors join him in memorializing. That revives a vicious late-Ming habit.

sentences.zh: 汝等票擬處分太重，可速召其來。」

translations.literal: Your draft punishments are too severe; summon him at once."
translations.idiomatic: Your proposed penalties are too harsh. Bring him in at once."

sentences.zh: 掞聞命趨入，免冠謝。

translations.literal: On hearing the order Shan hurried in, removed his cap, and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Shan hurried in, removed his cap, and apologized.

sentences.zh: 上招掞跪禦榻前，語良久，秘，人不能知。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Shan to kneel before the imperial couch and spoke with him at length in secret; no one could know what was said.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him kneel before the couch and spoke with him at length in private. No one else learned what was said.

sentences.zh: 六十年春，群臣請賀萬壽，上勿許。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixtieth year the officials asked to celebrate his longevity; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1721 the court asked to celebrate his birthday, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 掞复疏前事，請釋二阿哥，語加激切。

translations.literal: Shan again memorialized on the earlier matter, asking that the Second Prince be released; his language grew sharply urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Shan memorialized again on the same issue, urging release of the Second Prince in increasingly forceful terms.

sentences.zh: 既而御史陶彝等十二人連名入奏，上疑出掞意，大怒，召諸王大臣，降旨責掞植黨希榮，且謂：「錫爵在明神宗時，力奏建儲，泰昌在位，未及數月，天啟庸懦，天下大亂，至愍帝而不能守。

translations.literal: Soon after, Censors Tao Yi and eleven others jointly memorialized. The emperor suspected this came from Shan's instigation, was greatly angered, summoned the princes and high ministers, and issued an edict rebuking Shan for forming factions and seeking glory, saying: "Xijue in the Ming under Shenzong strongly urged establishing an heir. Taichang reigned less than a few months; Tianqi was weak and timid; the realm fell into great disorder, until Chongzhen could not hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Then Censors Tao Yi and eleven others submitted a joint memorial. Suspecting Shan had orchestrated it, the emperor flew into a rage, summoned the princes and senior ministers, and rebuked Shan for faction-building and ambition. He said: "Under the Ming Shenzong, Xijue pressed hard for an heir. Taichang reigned only months. Tianqi was weak, the realm collapsed, and even Chongzhen could not hold the state.

sentences.zh: 明之亡，錫爵不能辭其罪。

translations.literal: For the fall of the Ming, Xijue cannot escape blame.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue cannot escape blame for the fall of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 掞以朕為神宗乎？

translations.literal: Does Shan take Me for Shenzong?
translations.idiomatic: Does Shan take me for Shenzong?

sentences.zh: 朕初無誅大臣之意，大臣自取其死，朕亦無如何。」

translations.literal: I had no initial intent to execute great ministers; the ministers bring death upon themselves, and I can do nothing about it."
translations.idiomatic: I never meant to kill a great minister. If ministers court their own ruin, there is little I can do."

sentences.zh: 令王大臣傳旨詰掞，令回奏。

translations.literal: He ordered the princes and ministers to convey the edict interrogating Shan and to require a written reply.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the princes and ministers to question Shan and demand a written reply.

sentences.zh: 時舉朝失色，無敢與筆硯者。

translations.literal: At the time the whole court turned pale; none dared supply him brush and ink.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court was stricken. No one dared give him brush and ink.

sentences.zh: 掞就宮門階石上裂紙，以唾濡墨，奏言：「臣伏見宋仁宗為一代賢君，而晚年立儲猶豫，其時名臣如范鎮、包拯等，皆交章切諫，鬚髮為白。

translations.literal: Shan tore paper on the palace gate steps, moistened ink with saliva, and memorialized: "Your servant has observed that Emperor Renzong of Song was an exemplary ruler of his age, yet in his later years he hesitated over establishing an heir; eminent ministers such as Fan Zhen and Bao Zheng all submitted urgent joint remonstrances until their hair turned white.
translations.idiomatic: On the palace steps Shan tore paper and wrote with saliva for ink. He said: "I observe that Song Renzong was a sage ruler, yet even he hesitated over the heir in his later years. Ministers such as Fan Zhen and Bao Zheng remonstrated in urgent memorial after memorial until their hair turned white.

sentences.zh: 臣愚，信書太篤，妄思效法古人，實未嘗妄嗾台臣共為此奏。」

translations.literal: Your servant is foolish and trusted the histories too deeply, rashly thinking to imitate the ancients; I truly did not rashly incite censors to make this memorial together."
translations.idiomatic: I am foolish and trusted the histories too much. I rashly hoped to follow the ancients. I did not incite the censors to join in this memorial."

sentences.zh: 奏上，越五日，詔緩議罪，與諸御史俱赴西陲軍前效力。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, five days later an edict suspended deliberation on punishment; he and the censors were all sent to serve at the western frontier army.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later the emperor suspended punishment and ordered Shan and the censors to serve at the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 因掞年老，責其子奕清代往，為父贖罪。

translations.literal: Because Shan was old, his son Yiqing was ordered to go in his place to redeem his father's offense.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shan was elderly, his son Yiqing was sent in his stead to atone for him.

sentences.zh: 先是，掞嘗密奏請減蘇、松浮糧，言至剴切，疏久留中。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shan had secretly memorialized to reduce the excess grain levies of Suzhou and Songjiang; his words were most earnest, but the memorial long remained withheld.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had secretly asked to cut the excess grain levies in Suzhou and Songjiang. His plea was earnest, but the memorial had long been held back.

sentences.zh: 至是忤旨，乃與建儲奏疏一併擲還。

translations.literal: Now, having offended the imperial will, both that and the heir-establishment memorial were thrown back together.
translations.idiomatic: Now, having offended the throne, both that memorial and the heir memorial were returned together.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，上自熱河還京師。

translations.literal: That winter the emperor returned from Rehe to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the emperor returned from Rehe to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 掞迎駕石槽，上望見，遣內侍慰問。

translations.literal: Shan met the imperial procession at Shicao; the emperor saw him from afar and sent a eunuch to console him.
translations.idiomatic: Shan met the procession at Shicao. The emperor saw him from afar and sent a eunuch with words of comfort.

sentences.zh: 六十一年元旦，諸大臣表賀，未列掞名，上發表命列名以進。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the sixty-first year the ministers presented congratulatory memorials without listing Shan's name; the emperor returned the memorial and ordered his name included before resubmission.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of 1722 the ministers' congratulatory memorial omitted Shan's name. The emperor returned it and ordered his name added.

sentences.zh: 翌日，賜宴太和殿，再召見西暖閣，賜坐，慰諭有加。

translations.literal: The next day he was granted a banquet in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, summoned again to the West Warm Pavilion, given a seat, and comforted with added kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was feasted in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, summoned again to the West Warm Pavilion, given a seat, and warmly reassured.

sentences.zh: 尋起原官，視事如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was restored to his former office and administered affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored to his former post and resumed duty as before.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，以老乞休，世宗降旨褒嘉，以原官致仕，仍留京師備顧問。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, citing age he requested retirement; the Shizong Emperor issued an edict of praise, allowed him to retire with his former rank, and kept him in the capital for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1723 he asked to retire on account of age. The Yongzheng Emperor praised him in an edict, let him retire at his former rank, and kept him in Beijing as an adviser.

sentences.zh: 三年，上諭閣臣云：「王掞向人言，曾在聖祖前奏免蘇、松浮糧，未蒙允行。

translations.literal: In the third year the emperor told the Grand Secretariat: "Wang Shan has told others that he once memorialized before the late emperor to exempt Suzhou and Songjiang excess grain levies, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1725 the emperor told the Grand Secretariat: "Wang Shan has told others that he once asked the late emperor to cut the excess grain levies in Suzhou and Songjiang, but was not granted his request.

sentences.zh: 朕查閱宮中並無此奏。」

translations.literal: I have searched the palace archives and there is no such memorial."
translations.idiomatic: I have searched the palace archives and found no such memorial."

sentences.zh: 因責掞藉事沽名，並涉其子奕清、奕鴻諂附年羹堯，目為奸巧，乃遣奕鴻與奕清同在軍前效力。

translations.literal: He therefore rebuked Shan for trading on events to seek reputation, and implicated his sons Yiqing and Yihong in fawning on Nian Gengyao, calling them crafty; he then sent Yihong and Yiqing alike to serve at the army front.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuked Shan for using the matter to seek fame and accused his sons Yiqing and Yihong of currying favor with Nian Gengyao, calling them deceitful. He sent both sons to serve at the front.

sentences.zh: 六年，掞卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Shan died, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In 1728 he died at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，奕清始請血阝於朝，賜祭葬如製。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong, Yiqing first petitioned the court for posthumous honors; imperial sacrifices and burial were granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1737 Yiqing first petitioned for posthumous honors at court, and state sacrifices and burial were granted by regulation.

sentences.zh: 奕清，字幼芬。

translations.literal: Yiqing, style Youfen.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing, whose style was Youfen.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the thirtieth year of Kangxi; selected as Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1691 he became a metropolitan graduate and entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 歷官詹事。

translations.literal: He served successively as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 代父赴軍，歷駐忒斯、阿達拖羅海。

translations.literal: He went to the army in his father's stead and was stationed at Tesi and Adatuoluohai.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the frontier in his father's place and was posted at Tesi and Adatuoluohai.

sentences.zh: 奕清體羸善病，處之晏然。

translations.literal: Yiqing was frail and prone to illness, yet bore it with calm composure.
translations.idiomatic: Frail and often ill, Yiqing bore his hardships with calm.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，命赴阿爾泰坐檯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng he was ordered to the Altai command post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1726 he was ordered to the Altai command post.

sentences.zh: 又十年，乾隆元年，召還，仍以詹事管少詹事。

translations.literal: After another ten years, in the first year of Qianlong he was recalled and again served as Grand Tutor while managing the Junior Tutor's duties.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later, in 1736, he was recalled and again served as Grand Tutor while acting as Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 乞假葬父，尋卒。

translations.literal: He asked leave to bury his father and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to bury his father and soon died.

sentences.zh: 奕鴻，字樹先。

translations.literal: Yihong, style Shuxian.
translations.idiomatic: Yihong, whose style was Shuxian.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十八年進士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the forty-eighth year of Kangxi; appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1709 he became a metropolitan graduate and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 歷湖南驛鹽、糧儲道。

translations.literal: He served as Hunan intendant of courier stations and salt, and grain storage commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Hunan intendant for courier stations and salt, and as grain storage commissioner.

sentences.zh: 奕清赴軍，奕鴻盡斥其產與俱。

translations.literal: When Yiqing went to the army, Yihong sold off all his property and went with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yiqing went to the frontier, Yihong sold everything he owned and went with him.

sentences.zh: 後命赴烏里雅蘇台效力。

translations.literal: Later he was ordered to serve at Uliastai.
translations.idiomatic: He was later ordered to serve at Uliastai.

sentences.zh: 居邊十年，與奕清同釋還，官四川川東道。

translations.literal: After ten years on the frontier he was released with Yiqing and appointed Sichuan Eastern Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years on the frontier he was released with Yiqing and appointed intendant of eastern Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 引疾歸，卒。

translations.literal: He retired on grounds of illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on grounds of illness and died.

sentences.zh: 勞之辨，字書升，浙江石門人。

translations.literal: Lao Zhibian, style Shusheng, was a native of Shimen in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lao Zhibian, whose style was Shusheng, came from Shimen in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年進士，選庶吉士，授戶部主事，遷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the third year of Kangxi; selected as Hanlin bachelor, appointed secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and promoted to director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1664 he became a metropolitan graduate, entered the Hanlin Academy, was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and was promoted to director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 出為山東提學道僉事，報滿，左都御史魏象樞特疏薦之，遷貴州糧驛道參議。

translations.literal: He went out as Shandong educational commissioner vice intendant; when his term ended, Censor-in-Chief of the Left Wei Xiangshu specially memorialized to recommend him, and he was transferred to Guizhou grain and courier commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as educational vice intendant in Shandong. When his term ended, Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Xiangshu specially recommended him, and he was made Guizhou grain and courier commissioner.

sentences.zh: 師方下雲南，羽書旁午，之辨安設驛馬以利塘報；

translations.literal: The army was then advancing into Yunnan; urgent dispatches came incessantly. Zhibian arranged relay horses to speed courier reports;
translations.idiomatic: As the army advanced into Yunnan, urgent dispatches poured in. Zhibian set up relay horses to speed courier reports;

sentences.zh: 復以軍米運自湖南，苦累夫役，白大府停運，就地採購，供億無匱。

translations.literal: also, because army grain was transported from Hunan and burdened corvée laborers, he reported to the provincial authorities to halt transport and purchase locally; supplies were never exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Army grain was being hauled from Hunan and crushing the laborers. He persuaded the provincial authorities to stop the transport and buy locally, and supplies never ran short.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，擢通政使參議，遷兵部督捕理事官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Transmission Office and transferred to the Ministry of War's supervisor of bandit suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In 1685 he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Transmission Office and transferred to the Ministry of War post supervising bandit suppression.

sentences.zh: 連遭親喪。

translations.literal: He suffered bereavements in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He suffered several bereavements in succession.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 洊擢左副都御史，數有建白。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and often offered constructive proposals.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and often offered constructive proposals.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，皇太子允礽既廢，上日夕憂懣。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year, after Crown Prince Yunreng had been deposed, the emperor was day and night distressed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1708, after Crown Prince Yunreng was deposed, the emperor was day and night in distress.

sentences.zh: 既，有復儲意，王大臣合疏保奏，命留中。

translations.literal: Afterward he had thoughts of restoring the heir; princes and high ministers jointly memorialized in support, but the order was to hold the memorial back.
translations.idiomatic: He then considered restoring the heir. Princes and senior ministers jointly memorialized in support, but the emperor withheld the memorial.

sentences.zh: 旋諭廷臣：「俟廢太子疾瘳，教養有成，朕自有旨，諸王大臣不得多瀆。」

translations.literal: Soon he instructed the court: "Wait until the deposed crown prince's illness is cured and his upbringing is complete; I shall have my own decree. Princes and high ministers must not repeat such importunity."
translations.idiomatic: He soon told the court: "Wait until the deposed crown prince recovers and his upbringing is complete. I will issue my own decree. Princes and ministers must not press the matter again."

sentences.zh: 十二月，之辨密奏曰：「皇上之於皇太子，分則君臣，親則父子。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Zhibian secretly memorialized: "Between Your Majesty and the crown prince, in rank you are sovereign and subject, in affection father and son.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zhibian secretly memorialized: "Between Your Majesty and the crown prince, in office you are sovereign and subject, in affection father and son.

sentences.zh: 皇太子初以疾獲戾，今疾已平復。

translations.literal: The crown prince at first offended through illness; now his illness has fully recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince first gave offense through illness, but his illness has now fully recovered.

sentences.zh: 孝友之本懷，固由至性；

translations.literal: The fundamental feelings of filial piety and brotherly love surely spring from his deepest nature;
translations.idiomatic: His filial and brotherly heart surely springs from his deepest nature;

sentences.zh: 肅雍之儀表，久系群心。

translations.literal: his dignified and harmonious bearing has long held the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: and his dignified bearing has long held the hearts of the people.

sentences.zh: 乞速渙新綸，收回成詔，敕部擇吉早正東宮，佈告中外，俾天下曉然知聖人舉動，仁至義盡，大公無私。

translations.literal: I beg that a new edict be swiftly issued, the completed decree withdrawn, and the ministries ordered to choose an auspicious day soon to install the Eastern Palace, announcing it within and without, so all under Heaven may clearly know that the sage's actions are benevolence to the utmost and righteousness complete, great and impartial without private bias.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to issue a new edict at once, withdraw the completed decree, and order the ministries to choose an auspicious day to restore the Eastern Palace and proclaim it at home and abroad, so all under Heaven may see that the sage's act is fully benevolent, fully righteous, and wholly without private bias.

sentences.zh: 事莫有重於此者。

translations.literal: There is no matter weightier than this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing is more important than this.

sentences.zh: 今八荒清晏，一統車書，值星紀初《辶週》，光華復旦，七廟將行大祫，萬國於以朝正。

translations.literal: Now the eight directions are tranquil, chariots and books are unified; at the opening of a new sexagenary cycle glory returns at dawn; the seven temples are about to perform the great triennial collation; the myriad states will thereby align in court.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is at peace and unified. A new sexagenary cycle is beginning, glory is renewed, the seven temples are about to hold the great triennial collation, and the myriad states will come to court.

sentences.zh: 皇上以孝慈治天下，方且稱壽母萬年之觴，集麟趾繁昌之慶；

translations.literal: Your Majesty governs all under Heaven with filial piety and compassion, and is just now raising the cup of ten thousand years for the empress dowager's longevity, gathering the blessings of many sons and flourishing posterity;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty governs the realm with filial piety and compassion, and is even now toasting the empress dowager's longevity and gathering blessings of many sons and flourishing heirs;

sentences.zh: 而顧使前星虛位，震子未寧，聖心得無有遺憾乎？

translations.literal: yet would you leave the Fore Star's place empty and the heir of Zhen unsettled—can the sage heart be without regret?
translations.idiomatic: yet would you leave the heir's place empty and the heir of Zhen unsettled? Can the sage heart be without regret?

sentences.zh: 臣年已七十，報主之日無多，知無不言，統望乾斷速行。

translations.literal: Your servant is already seventy; days to repay my lord are few; knowing, I speak without reserve; I altogether hope for Your decisive judgment and swift action.
translations.idiomatic: I am already seventy, and have few days left to serve my lord. I speak without reserve and beg Your Majesty to decide and act at once.

sentences.zh: 自此以往，皇上待皇太子與諸皇子，尤原均之以恩，範之以禮，則宜君宜王之美，不難上媲成周，遠超百代。

translations.literal: From now on, if Your Majesty treats the crown prince and all the princes with especial evenness in grace and molding in ritual, then the beauty of being fit to rule as lord and king would not be hard to match the Zhou of Cheng, and would far surpass a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, if Your Majesty treats the crown prince and all the princes with equal grace and molds them with ritual, the virtue of a true sovereign would rival the Zhou of Cheng and surpass a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 至萬不得已而裁之以法，則非臣之所敢言也。」

translations.literal: As for resorting to law only when absolutely unavoidable—that is not what your servant dares speak of."
translations.idiomatic: As for resorting to law only when there is no other choice—that is not what I dare say."

sentences.zh: 疏入，上不懌，斥為奸詭，命奪官，逮赴刑部笞四十，逐回原籍。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted the emperor was displeased, denounced him as crafty and deceitful, ordered his office stripped, had him taken to the Ministry of Justice for forty blows of the rod, and banished to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: When it was submitted the emperor was displeased, called him crafty and deceitful, stripped his office, had him flogged forty strokes at the Ministry of Justice, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，赴京祝萬壽，復原秩。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he went to the capital to offer longevity congratulations and was restored to his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1713 he went to Beijing to offer birthday congratulations and was restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒於家。

translations.literal: The following year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died at home.

sentences.zh: 硃天保，字九如，滿洲鑲白旗人，兵部侍郎硃都訥子。

translations.literal: Zhu Tianbao, style Jiuru, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner and son of Vice Minister of War Zhu Dune.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tianbao, whose style was Jiuru, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner and the son of Vice Minister of War Zhu Dune.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十二年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the fifty-second year of Kangxi; selected as Hanlin bachelor and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In 1713 he became a metropolitan graduate, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was made a reviser.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，典山東鄉試。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he presided over the Shandong provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1717 he presided over the Shandong provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 五十七年正月，疏請復立二阿哥允礽為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifty-seventh year he memorialized to restore the Second Prince Yunreng as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1718 he memorialized to restore the Second Prince Yunreng as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時允礽廢已久，儲位未定，貝勒允禩覬得立，揆敘、王鴻緒等左右之，欲陰害允礽。

translations.literal: Yunreng had long been deposed and the succession was unsettled; Prince Yunsi coveted the position; Kui Xu, Wang Hongxu, and others supported him and wished secretly to harm Yunreng.
translations.idiomatic: Yunreng had long been deposed and the succession unsettled. Prince Yunsi coveted the throne, and Kui Xu, Wang Hongxu, and others backed him and wished secretly to harm Yunreng.

sentences.zh: 硃天保憂之，具疏上，略曰：「二阿哥雖以疾廢，然其過失良由習於驕抗，左右小人誘導之故。

translations.literal: Zhu Tianbao was troubled by this and submitted a full memorial, saying in summary: "Although the Second Prince was deposed because of illness, his faults truly arose from habituating to arrogance and defiance and from petty men at his side who led him astray.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tianbao was troubled and submitted a memorial, saying in part: "Although the Second Prince was deposed for illness, his faults came from arrogance and from petty men who led him astray.

sentences.zh: 若遣碩儒名臣為之羽翼，左右佞幸盡皆罷斥，則潛德日彰，猶可復問安侍膳之歡。

translations.literal: If eminent scholars and renowned ministers were sent to support him and all flatterers at his side were dismissed, his hidden virtue would daily shine forth, and he could still regain the joy of inquiring after Your health and attending at meals.
translations.idiomatic: If eminent scholars were sent to guide him and all flatterers were removed, his virtue would daily grow plain, and he could again share the joy of attending Your Majesty at meals.

sentences.zh: 儲位重大，未可移置如釭，恐有籓臣傍為覬覦，則天家骨肉之禍，有不可勝言者。」

translations.literal: The heir's position is weighty and must not be shifted like a cooking pot; I fear vassal ministers may covet it from the side, and then calamity among the imperial kin would be beyond telling."
translations.idiomatic: The heir's place is weighty and must not be shifted lightly. I fear vassal ministers may covet it, and then the calamity among the imperial kin would be beyond words."

sentences.zh: 疏成，以父在，慮同禍，徘徊未即上。

translations.literal: When the memorial was finished, because his father was alive he feared shared disaster and hesitated without submitting it at once.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished, fearing his father would share the blame, he hesitated and did not submit it at once.

sentences.zh: 硃都訥察其情，趣之入告。

translations.literal: Zhu Dune perceived his state and urged him to enter and report it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Dune saw his hesitation and urged him to submit it.

sentences.zh: 時上方幸湯山，硃天保早出德勝門，群鴉阻馬前，硃天保揮之去。

translations.literal: The emperor was then at Tangshan Hot Springs; Zhu Tianbao left early through Desheng Gate; a flock of crows blocked before his horse, and Zhu Tianbao waved them away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at Tangshan. Zhu Tianbao left early through Desheng Gate. A flock of crows blocked his horse, and he waved them away.

sentences.zh: 疏上，上欷歔久之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted the emperor sighed for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived the emperor sighed for a long while.

sentences.zh: 阿靈阿，允禩黨也，媒孽之曰：「硃天保為異日希寵地。」

translations.literal: Aling'a, a member of Yunsi's faction, slandered him, saying: "Zhu Tianbao is staking out ground to seek favor in days to come."
translations.idiomatic: Aling'a, a member of Yunsi's faction, slandered him, saying, "Zhu Tianbao is currying favor for the future."

sentences.zh: 上怒，於行宮禦門召問曰：「爾雲二阿哥仁孝，何由知之？」

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and summoned him for questioning at the imperial gate of the traveling palace: "You say the Second Prince is benevolent and filial—how do you know?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and summoned him at the palace gate: "You say the Second Prince is benevolent and filial. How do you know?"

sentences.zh: 硃天保以聞父語對。

translations.literal: Zhu Tianbao answered with what he had heard from his father.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tianbao answered with what his father had told him.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「爾父在官時，二阿哥本無疾，學問弓馬皆可觀。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When your father was in office the Second Prince had no illness at all; his learning and archery and horsemanship were all commendable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When your father was in office the Second Prince had no illness. His learning, archery, and horsemanship were all commendable.

sentences.zh: 後得瘋疾，舉動乖張，嘗立朕前辱罵徐元夢。

translations.literal: Later he contracted madness; his conduct was perverse; he once stood before Me and reviled Xu Yuanmeng.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went mad. His conduct became erratic. He once stood before me and reviled Xu Yuanmeng.

sentences.zh: 於伯叔之子往往以不可道之言肆詈，爾知之乎？

translations.literal: Toward his uncles' sons he often poured forth unspeakable abuse—do you know this?
translations.idiomatic: He often hurled unspeakable abuse at his uncles' sons. Do you know this?

sentences.zh: 爾又云二阿哥聖而益聖，賢而益賢，爾從何而知？」

translations.literal: You also say the Second Prince grows ever more sage and ever more worthy—from what do you know?"
translations.idiomatic: You also say he grows ever more sage and worthy. How do you know?"

sentences.zh: 硃天保亦以父聞之守者對。

translations.literal: Zhu Tianbao likewise answered with what his father had heard from the guards.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tianbao again answered with what his father had heard from the guards.

sentences.zh: 詰其姓名，不能答。

translations.literal: When their names were demanded he could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When asked their names he could not answer.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕以爾陳奏此大事，遣人傳問，或將爾言遺漏，故親訊爾。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Because you reported this great matter, I might have sent someone to question you and your words been lost; therefore I questioned you in person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Because you reported this great matter, I questioned you in person lest your words be lost in transmission.

sentences.zh: 爾無知稚子，數語即窮，必有同謀者。」

translations.literal: You are an ignorant youth; a few words and you are at an end—there must be co-conspirators."
translations.idiomatic: You are an ignorant youth. A few questions and you are undone. There must be co-conspirators."

sentences.zh: 硃天保對父與婿戴保同謀，遂逮硃都訥、戴保。

translations.literal: Zhu Tianbao answered that his father and son-in-law Dai Bao had conspired together; Zhu Dune and Dai Bao were then arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tianbao said his father and son-in-law Dai Bao had conspired with him, and Zhu Dune and Dai Bao were arrested.

sentences.zh: 上复禦門召問曰：「二阿哥因病拘禁，朕猶望其痊癒，故复釋放，父子相見。

translations.literal: The emperor again summoned them for questioning at the imperial gate: "The Second Prince was confined because of illness; I still hoped he would recover, so I released him again and father and son met.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again questioned them at the gate: "The Second Prince was confined for illness. I still hoped he would recover, released him, and father and son met.

sentences.zh: 教訓不悛，始復拘禁。

translations.literal: He would not reform under instruction, and only then was he confined again.
translations.idiomatic: He would not reform under instruction, and only then was he confined again.

sentences.zh: 二阿哥以礬水作書與普奇，屬其保舉為大將軍，並謂齊世、札拉克圖皆當為將軍。

translations.literal: The Second Prince wrote with alum water to Puqi, asking him to recommend him as great general, and also said Qishi and Zhilaketu should both become generals.
translations.idiomatic: The Second Prince wrote in invisible ink to Puqi, asking him to recommend him as great general and saying Qishi and Zhilaketu should also become generals.

sentences.zh: 朕遣內侍往詢，自承為親筆。

translations.literal: I sent a palace attendant to inquire, and he admitted it was in his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: I sent a palace attendant to inquire, and he admitted it was in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 此事爾知之否？」

translations.literal: Do you know of this matter?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you know of this?"

sentences.zh: 硃都訥自稱妄奏，應萬死。

translations.literal: Zhu Dune declared he had memorialized rashly and deserved ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Dune said he had memorialized rashly and deserved death.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「爾奏引戾太子為比。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your memorial cited Crown Prince Li as a comparison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your memorial cited Crown Prince Li as a comparison.

sentences.zh: 戾太子父子間隔，朕於二阿哥常遣內監往視，賜食賜物。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Li and his father were estranged; toward the Second Prince I constantly send eunuchs to visit and bestow food and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Li and his father were estranged. Toward the Second Prince I constantly send eunuchs to visit and give food and gifts.

sentences.zh: 今二阿哥顏貌豐滿，其子七八人，朕常留養宮中，何得比戾太子？

translations.literal: Now the Second Prince's face is full and robust; he has seven or eight sons whom I often keep and raise in the palace—how can he be compared to Crown Prince Li?
translations.idiomatic: Now the Second Prince looks full and healthy. He has seven or eight sons whom I often keep in the palace. How can he be compared to Crown Prince Li?

sentences.zh: 爾又稱二阿哥為費揚古陷害。

translations.literal: You also said the Second Prince was framed by Fei Yanggu.
translations.idiomatic: You also said the Second Prince was framed by Fei Yanggu.

sentences.zh: 費揚古乃功臣，病篤時，朕親臨視，沒後遣二阿哥往奠。

translations.literal: Fei Yanggu was a meritorious minister; when he was gravely ill I personally visited him, and after his death I sent the Second Prince to offer mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yanggu was a meritorious minister. When he was gravely ill I visited him in person, and after his death I sent the Second Prince to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 爾何得妄言？

translations.literal: How can you speak so rashly?
translations.idiomatic: How can you speak so rashly?

sentences.zh: 爾希僥倖取大富貴，以朕有疾，必不親訊。

translations.literal: You hoped by chance to gain great wealth and honor, thinking that because I am ill I would certainly not question you in person.
translations.idiomatic: You hoped by chance to win great wealth and honor, thinking that because I am ill I would not question you in person.

sentences.zh: 今爾始知當死乎？」

translations.literal: Now do you know you deserve death?"
translations.idiomatic: Now do you know you deserve death?"

sentences.zh: 辭連硃都訥婿常賚及金寶、齊世、萃泰等，並逮訊議罪。

translations.literal: The case implicated Zhu Dune's son-in-law Chang Sai and Jin Bao, Qishi, Cuitai, and others; all were arrested, questioned, and sentenced.
translations.idiomatic: The case implicated Zhu Dune's son-in-law Chang Sai, Jin Bao, Qishi, Cuitai, and others. All were arrested, questioned, and sentenced.

sentences.zh: 硃天保、戴保皆坐斬。

translations.literal: Zhu Tianbao and Dai Bao were both sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tianbao and Dai Bao were both sentenced to decapitation.

sentences.zh: 硃都訥與常賚、金寶皆免死荷校，齊世拘禁，萃泰奪官。

translations.literal: Zhu Dune, Chang Sai, and Jin Bao were all spared death but made to wear the cangue; Qishi was confined; Cuitai was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Dune, Chang Sai, and Jin Bao were spared death but made to wear the cangue. Qishi was confined and Cuitai was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 陶彝，順天大興人。

translations.literal: Tao Yi was a native of Daxing in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Yi came from Daxing in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十九年進士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the thirty-ninth year of Kangxi; appointed secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1700 he became a metropolitan graduate and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to director.

sentences.zh: 考選廣西道御史，巡視兩浙鹽政。

translations.literal: Selected by examination as censor of the Guangxi Circuit and assigned to inspect the salt administration of the two Zhe provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as censor of the Guangxi Circuit and assigned to inspect salt administration in the two Zhe provinces.

sentences.zh: 六十年三月，彝與同官任坪、范長發、鄒圖雲、陳嘉猷、王允晉、李允符、範允、高玢、高怡、趙成麃、孫紹曾合疏奏曰：「皇上深恩厚德，浹洽人心。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixtieth year Yi and his colleagues Ren Ping, Fan Changfa, Zou Tuyun, Chen Jiayou, Wang Yunjin, Li Yunfu, Fan Yun, Gao Bin, Gao Yi, Zhao Chengbiao, and Sun Shaozeng jointly memorialized: "Your Majesty's deep grace and thick virtue saturate the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1721 Yi and his colleagues Ren Ping, Fan Changfa, Zou Tuyun, Chen Jiayou, Wang Yunjin, Li Yunfu, Fan Yun, Gao Bin, Gao Yi, Zhao Chengbiao, and Sun Shaozeng jointly memorialized: "Your Majesty's deep grace and great virtue fill the hearts of the people.

sentences.zh: 茲逢六十年，景運方新，普天率土，歡欣鼓舞，而建儲一事，尤為鉅典。

translations.literal: Now we meet the sixtieth year; the auspicious fortune is newly renewed; all under Heaven within the four seas rejoice and exult; yet establishing the heir is especially a great ritual.
translations.idiomatic: We mark the sixtieth year, a renewed age of fortune, and all under Heaven rejoices. Yet establishing the heir is the greatest ritual of all.

sentences.zh: 懇獨斷宸衷，早定儲位。」

translations.literal: We earnestly beg Your solitary decision from the imperial heart to fix the heir's place early."
translations.idiomatic: We earnestly beg Your Majesty to decide in Your own heart and fix the succession soon."

sentences.zh: 疏入，下內閣。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted it was sent down to the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When it was submitted it was sent to the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時大學士王掞正密疏請建儲。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Secretary Wang Shan was secretly memorializing to establish an heir.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Grand Secretary Wang Shan was secretly memorializing to name an heir.

sentences.zh: 後數日，彝等疏又上，上震怒，斥掞植黨希榮。

translations.literal: Several days later Yi's memorial was submitted again; the emperor was greatly angered and rebuked Shan for forming factions and seeking glory.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Yi's memorial was submitted again. The emperor was enraged and rebuked Shan for faction-building and ambition.

sentences.zh: 於是王大臣奏請奪掞及諸御史官，從重治罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon the princes and high ministers memorialized to strip Shan and the censors of office and punish them severely.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and senior ministers then asked to strip Shan and the censors of office and punish them severely.

sentences.zh: 越日，諭廷臣曰：「王掞及御史陶彝等妄行陳奏，俱稱為國為君。

translations.literal: The next day he instructed the court: "Wang Shan and Censor Tao Yi and others rashly memorialized, all claiming to act for the state and the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he told the court: "Wang Shan and Censor Tao Yi and others rashly memorialized, all claiming to act for the state and the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 今西陲用兵，為人臣者，正宜滅此朝食。

translations.literal: Now war is waged on the western frontier; as subjects they ought rather to swallow the enemy this very morning.
translations.idiomatic: War is now on the western frontier. As subjects they ought to swallow the enemy this very morning.

sentences.zh: 可暫緩議罰，如八旗滿洲文官例，俱委署額外章京，遣往軍前效力贖罪。」

translations.literal: Punishment may be suspended for the moment; following the precedent for Manchu civil officials of the Eight Banners, let them all be appointed acting extra clerks and sent to the army front to serve and redeem their guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Punishment may wait. Following the precedent for Manchu civil officials of the Eight Banners, appoint them acting extra clerks and send them to the front to serve and redeem their guilt."

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，世宗以諸御史不諳國體，心本無他，詔釋歸，以原職休致還籍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng the Shizong Emperor, considering that the censors did not understand statecraft but had no other intent at heart, ordered them released to retire at their former ranks and return home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1726 the Yongzheng Emperor, judging that the censors did not understand statecraft but meant no harm, ordered them released to retire at their former ranks and return home.

sentences.zh: 坪，字坦公，山東高密人。

translations.literal: Ping, style Tangong, was a native of Gaomi in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Ping, whose style was Tangong, came from Gaomi in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十年進士。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the thirtieth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1691 he became a metropolitan graduate.

sentences.zh: 自刑部郎中考選山西道御史，轉掌陝西道。

translations.literal: From director in the Ministry of Justice he was selected by examination as censor of the Shanxi Circuit and transferred to head the Shaanxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: From director in the Ministry of Justice he was selected as censor of the Shanxi Circuit and transferred to head the Shaanxi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 赴軍，駐忒斯河。

translations.literal: He went to the army and was stationed on the Tesi River.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the army and was stationed on the Tesi River.

sentences.zh: 大漠荒寒，盛夏冰雪，坪處之怡然。

translations.literal: The great desert was desolate and cold; in midsummer there was ice and snow; Ping bore it with calm ease.
translations.idiomatic: The desert was desolate and cold, with ice and snow even in midsummer, yet Ping bore it calmly.

sentences.zh: 及歸，閉戶讀書，終老於家。

translations.literal: When he returned he shut his doors to read and ended his days at home.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned he shut his doors to study and lived out his days at home.

sentences.zh: 長發，字廷舒，浙江秀水人。

translations.literal: Changfa, style Tingshu, was a native of Xiushui in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Changfa, whose style was Tingshu, came from Xiushui in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十三年進士，授南城知縣。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the thirty-third year of Kangxi; appointed magistrate of Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In 1694 he became a metropolitan graduate and was appointed magistrate of Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 行取禮部主事，考選廣西道御史，轉掌浙江道。

translations.literal: Selected for promotion to secretary in the Ministry of Rites; chosen by examination as censor of the Guangxi Circuit; transferred to head the Zhejiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected for the Ministry of Rites, chosen as censor of the Guangxi Circuit, and transferred to head the Zhejiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 遣戍，予額外主事銜，隨都統圖臘赴征西將軍營。

translations.literal: Banished to frontier service, he was given the brevet rank of extra secretary and followed Commander Tula to the camp of the Western Expedition general.
translations.idiomatic: Banished to frontier service, he was given the brevet rank of extra secretary and followed Commander Tula to the Western Expedition general's camp.

sentences.zh: 還，駐歸化城。

translations.literal: On return he was stationed at Guihua City.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was stationed at Guihua City.

sentences.zh: 後命赴察漢新台。

translations.literal: Later he was ordered to Chahan New Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He was later ordered to Chahan New Terrace.

sentences.zh: 歸，以原職休致。

translations.literal: When he returned he retired with his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned he retired at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 圖雲，字偉南，江西南城人。

translations.literal: Tuyun, style Weinan, was a native of Nancheng in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyun, whose style was Weinan, came from Nancheng in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十六年進士，授大竹知縣。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the thirty-sixth year of Kangxi; appointed magistrate of Dazhu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1697 he became a metropolitan graduate and was appointed magistrate of Dazhu.

sentences.zh: 行取禮部主事，考選河南道御史，轉掌山東道，巡視東城。

translations.literal: Selected for the Ministry of Rites as secretary; chosen by examination as censor of the Henan Circuit; transferred to head the Shandong Circuit and inspect the Eastern City.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected for the Ministry of Rites, chosen as censor of the Henan Circuit, transferred to head the Shandong Circuit, and assigned to inspect the Eastern City.

sentences.zh: 嘉猷，字讱叔，江南溧陽人。

translations.literal: Jiayou, style Renshu, was a native of Liyang in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou, whose style was Renshu, came from Liyang in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十九年進士。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the thirty-ninth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1700 he became a metropolitan graduate.

sentences.zh: 自吏部員外郎考選山西道御史。

translations.literal: From vice director in the Ministry of Personnel he was selected by examination as censor of the Shanxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: From vice director in the Ministry of Personnel he was selected as censor of the Shanxi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，王掞密請建儲。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year Wang Shan secretly memorialized to establish an heir.
translations.idiomatic: In 1717 Wang Shan secretly memorialized to name an heir.

sentences.zh: 未幾，嘉猷與同官八人亦合疏陳請，上疑之，掞幾獲罪，事具掞傳。

translations.literal: Before long Jiayou and eight colleagues also jointly memorialized in request; the emperor was suspicious; Shan nearly incurred punishment—the matter is fully set forth in Shan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Jiayou and eight colleagues jointly memorialized as well. The emperor was suspicious and Shan nearly fell. The matter is told fully in Shan's biography.

sentences.zh: 至是，嘉猷復與彝等申請，獲咎。

translations.literal: On this occasion Jiayou again joined Yi and others in petitioning and incurred blame.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion Jiayou again joined Yi and others in petitioning and was punished.

sentences.zh: 允晉，直隸清苑人。

translations.literal: Yunjin was a native of Qingyuan in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Yunjin came from Qingyuan in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十五年進士。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the forty-fifth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1706 he became a metropolitan graduate.

sentences.zh: 自戶部員外郎考選陝西道御史。

translations.literal: From vice director in the Ministry of Revenue he was selected by examination as censor of the Shaanxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: From vice director in the Ministry of Revenue he was selected as censor of the Shaanxi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 允符，字揆山，浙江嘉善人。

translations.literal: Yunfu, style Kuishan, was a native of Jiashan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yunfu, whose style was Kuishan, came from Jiashan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十六年舉人，授什邡知縣。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the twenty-sixth year of Kangxi; appointed magistrate of Shifang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1687 he passed the provincial examination and was appointed magistrate of Shifang.

sentences.zh: 行取江西道御史。

translations.literal: Selected for promotion as censor of the Jiangxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as censor of the Jiangxi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 允，字用賓，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Yun, style Yongbin, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun, whose style was Yongbin, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十九年進士，授安平知縣。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the thirty-ninth year of Kangxi; appointed magistrate of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: In 1700 he became a metropolitan graduate and was appointed magistrate of Anping.

sentences.zh: 行取工部主事，考選山東道御史。

translations.literal: Selected for the Ministry of Works as secretary; chosen by examination as censor of the Shandong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected for the Ministry of Works and chosen as censor of the Shandong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 玢，字荊襄，河南柘城人。

translations.literal: Bin, style Jingxiang, was a native of Zhecheng in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Bin, whose style was Jingxiang, came from Zhecheng in Henan.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十七年進士。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1688 he became a metropolitan graduate.

sentences.zh: 自禮部郎中考選廣東道御史，巡視東城。

translations.literal: From director in the Ministry of Rites he was selected by examination as censor of the Guangdong Circuit and assigned to inspect the Eastern City.
translations.idiomatic: From director in the Ministry of Rites he was selected as censor of the Guangdong Circuit and assigned to inspect the Eastern City.

sentences.zh: 謫戍忒斯軍營，運糧西藏。

translations.literal: Banished to garrison duty at the Tesi army camp, he transported grain to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Banished to the Tesi garrison, he transported grain to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 居塞上六年，著出塞集，備言屯戍之苦。

translations.literal: He lived on the frontier six years and wrote the Collection from Beyond the Pass, fully describing the hardships of garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on the frontier six years and wrote the Collection from Beyond the Pass, describing the hardships of garrison life in full.

sentences.zh: 釋歸，終於家。

translations.literal: Released and returned home, he died there.
translations.idiomatic: Released and sent home, he died there.

sentences.zh: 怡，字仲友，浙江武康人。

translations.literal: Yi, style Zhongyou, was a native of Wukang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yi, whose style was Zhongyou, came from Wukang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十七年進士，授長洲知縣。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi; appointed magistrate of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1688 he became a metropolitan graduate and was appointed magistrate of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 善聽訟，吏胥憚之。

translations.literal: He was skilled at hearing lawsuits; clerks and runners feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at hearing cases, and clerks and runners feared him.

sentences.zh: 尚書韓菼，怡師也，其姻黨繫獄，以菼故請恕，怡怒杖之。

translations.literal: Minister Han Tan was Yi's teacher; a kinsman of Tan's was imprisoned and asked forgiveness because of Tan; Yi angrily had him beaten with the rod.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Han Tan had been his teacher. A kinsman of Tan's was in prison and asked leniency on Tan's account. Yi angrily had him beaten.

sentences.zh: 選鄜州知州，行取工部主事。

translations.literal: Selected as prefect of Fuzhou; promoted by selection to secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as prefect of Fuzhou and then promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 考選山東道御史。

translations.literal: Chosen by examination as censor of the Shandong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen as censor of the Shandong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 謫戍時，年逾六十。

translations.literal: When banished to frontier garrison duty he was over sixty.
translations.idiomatic: When he was banished to frontier service he was over sixty.

sentences.zh: 以原職釋歸。

translations.literal: He was released and sent home with his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was released and sent home at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 赵成麃，字德培，江南吳縣人。

translations.literal: Zhao Chengbiao, style Depei, was a native of Wu County in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chengbiao, whose style was Depei, came from Wu County in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十七年舉人，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the forty-seventh year of Kangxi; appointed secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1708 he passed the provincial examination and was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 累遷兵部郎中，考選福建道御史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of War and chosen by examination as censor of the Fujian Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director in the Ministry of War and was chosen as censor of the Fujian Circuit.

sentences.zh: 紹曾，字二乾，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Shaozeng, style Erqian, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shaozeng, whose style was Erqian, came from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十五年舉人，授開縣知縣。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the twenty-fifth year of Kangxi; appointed magistrate of Kai County.
translations.idiomatic: In 1686 he passed the provincial examination and was appointed magistrate of Kai County.

sentences.zh: 行取戶部主事，授四川道御史。

translations.literal: Selected for the Ministry of Revenue as secretary; appointed censor of the Sichuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected for the Ministry of Revenue and appointed censor of the Sichuan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 赴軍，駐歸化城，地當孔道。

translations.literal: He went to the army and was stationed at Guihua City, on a major thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the army and was posted at Guihua City, on a major thoroughfare.

sentences.zh: 故事，徭役供張，取給於戍員。

translations.literal: By precedent corvée labor and supplies for official receptions were drawn from the garrison officers.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent corvée labor and supplies for official receptions were drawn from the garrison officers.

sentences.zh: 紹曾清介無馀資，困甚。

translations.literal: Shaozeng was upright and without surplus funds and was greatly distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shaozeng was upright and had no spare funds, and was greatly distressed.

sentences.zh: 迨釋還，卒於途。

translations.literal: When released and returning, he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When he was released and sent home, he died on the road.

sentences.zh: 又有邵璿，亦以疏請建儲獲罪。

translations.literal: There was also Shao Xuan, who likewise was punished for memorializing to establish an heir.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Shao Xuan, who was likewise punished for memorializing to name an heir.

sentences.zh: 璿，字璣亭，江南無錫人。

translations.literal: Xuan, style Jiting, was a native of Wuxi in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xuan, whose style was Jiting, came from Wuxi in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 自拔貢生授芮城知縣。

translations.literal: From a selected tribute student he was appointed magistrate of Ruicheng.
translations.idiomatic: From a selected tribute student he was appointed magistrate of Ruicheng.

sentences.zh: 行取工部主事，授江南道御史，掌登聞院，巡視北城。

translations.literal: Selected for the Ministry of Works as secretary; appointed censor of the Jiangnan Circuit, placed in charge of the Memorial Gate Office, and assigned to inspect the Northern City.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected for the Ministry of Works, appointed censor of the Jiangnan Circuit, placed in charge of the Memorial Gate Office, and assigned to inspect the Northern City.

sentences.zh: 六十年，遣戍軍前。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he was banished to garrison duty at the army front.
translations.idiomatic: In 1721 he was banished to service at the army front.

sentences.zh: 時同謫者十三人，圖雲、允符、成麃、璿皆死於塞外，而給事中劉堂，御史柴謙、吳鎬、程鑣續以言事謫，同時釋還，仍為十三人，世稱「十三言官」。

translations.literal: At the time thirteen were banished together; Tuyun, Yunfu, Chengbiao, and Xuan all died beyond the passes, while Supervising Secretary Liu Tang and Censors Chai Qian, Wu Hao, and Cheng Biao were in turn banished for speaking on affairs; when released at the same time they were still thirteen in number, and the age called them the "Thirteen Speaking Officials."
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen were banished together. Tuyun, Yunfu, Chengbiao, and Xuan all died beyond the passes. Supervising Secretary Liu Tang and Censors Chai Qian, Wu Hao, and Cheng Biao were later banished for remonstrance. When released together they were still thirteen, and the age called them the "Thirteen Speaking Officials."

sentences.zh: 堂，彭澤人。

translations.literal: Tang was a native of Pengze.
translations.idiomatic: Tang came from Pengze.

sentences.zh: 謙，仁和人。

translations.literal: Qian was a native of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Qian came from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 鎬，漢陽人。

translations.literal: Hao was a native of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hao came from Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 鑣，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Biao was a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Biao came from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 論曰：理密親王在儲位久，未聞顯有失德，而終遭廢黜，聖祖手詔，若有深痛鉅慝至不可言者。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Prince Limi long held the heir's position and no marked misconduct was heard of, yet in the end he suffered deposition; the sage ancestor's own edict seems to hold deep pain at a great evil beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Prince Limi long held the heir's place and no marked misconduct was heard of, yet he was deposed in the end. The Kangxi Emperor's own edict seems to hold a grief at some great evil beyond words.

sentences.zh: 夫以聖祖之仁明，而不克全監撫之重，終父子之恩，讒人罔極，靡所不至，甚矣！

translations.literal: That one so benevolent and clear-sighted as the sage ancestor could not fully fulfill the weight of overseeing and instructing, nor bring father-son affection to its end—slanderers without limit reaching everywhere—is extreme indeed!
translations.idiomatic: That the Kangxi Emperor, so benevolent and clear-sighted, could not fully fulfill the duty of overseeing and instructing the heir, nor bring father and son to reconciliation—slanderers reached everywhere without limit. How extreme it was!

sentences.zh: 掞力主復故，聖祖雖深罪之，固諒其無他心。

translations.literal: Shan strongly urged restoration of the former heir; though the sage ancestor punished him deeply, he surely understood he had no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: Shan strongly urged restoring the former heir. Though the Kangxi Emperor punished him severely, he surely understood Shan had no other intent.

sentences.zh: 勞之辨諫於初廢，大臣拜杖，已非故事；

translations.literal: Lao Zhibian remonstrated at the first deposition; great ministers beaten with the rod was already not precedent;
translations.idiomatic: Lao Zhibian remonstrated at the first deposition. Beating great ministers with the rod was already not precedent.

sentences.zh: 硃天保爭於再黜，遂以誅死，罪及其親。

translations.literal: Zhu Tianbao contended at the second dismissal and was then put to death by execution, guilt reaching his kin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tianbao contended at the second dismissal and was executed, guilt reaching his kin.

sentences.zh: 一則但責其沽名，一則深疑其受指，故譴有重輕歟？

translations.literal: In one case he was only rebuked for seeking reputation; in the other deeply suspected of taking direction—thus were the punishments light and heavy?
translations.idiomatic: In one case he was only rebuked for seeking reputation; in the other deeply suspected of acting on others' orders. Was that why the punishments differed in severity?

sentences.zh: 彝等但坐謫戍，已為寬典，拳拳效忠，固人臣之義也。

translations.literal: Yi and the others received only banishment to frontier garrison, already a lenient measure; earnest loyalty is indeed the duty of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and the others received only banishment to frontier service, already a lenient measure. Earnest loyalty is indeed a subject's duty.
